clue.text: Carry on praying aloud for this arty type?

definitions.text: Carry on praying aloud for this arty type?

parts.words: Carry on praying aloud for this arty type?
parts.note: said aloud, 'carry on praying' is 'carrion preying', which is how a scavenging bird feeds; graft on the cult of the arts and you have an eager consumer of culture

explanation.surface: Someone is told to keep at their prayers out loud, apparently for the sake of an artistic person.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a pun rather than a build: a vulture preys on carrion, so the sounds of 'carry on praying' summon the bird, and the arty type who devours culture is the phrase's other half.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for a person who hungrily consumes the arts, galleries, concerts and opera alike.

clue.text: Exile's condition when stuck: oh, cruel abandonment!

indicators.note: wild abandonment tosses these twelve letters about until they form a new phrase

explanation.surface: A banished person, trapped and miserable, cries out at being cruelly cast aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandonment' signals the anagram of STUCK OH CRUEL; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An exile suddenly living in an unfamiliar society suffers disorientation, the classic description of that unsettled state.

clue.text: Help given when reading Latin, say, at university

parts.note: leg- is the Latin stem for reading, as in legere, to read
to be up is to be in residence at university

explanation.surface: A student gets assistance with Latin texts while at college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link. Being UP means being at university, especially Oxford or Cambridge, in British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg-up is a boost or helping hand, literally a lift onto a horse.

clue.text: Put out man not working with child

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the three letters are rearranged

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
duff is British slang for broken or useless

explanation.surface: A man without a job is upset at having a child to support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' looks like a definition meaning annoyed, but 'out' scrambles PUT into UPT. The answer is British slang for pregnant.
explanation.definitionFit: The expression is British slang for being pregnant, which is what carrying a child means.

clue.text: Soup up in Franco-Chinese establishment

parts.note: the French word for in is en, French being signalled by Franco-
the Han are China's majority people, so Han stands for Chinese
CE, the Church of England, is the Established Church

explanation.surface: Food is served in a restaurant mixing French and Chinese cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Franco-' marks 'in' as French, giving EN, while the Chinese half supplies HAN. 'Establishment' is CE, the Church of England, England's state church.
explanation.definitionFit: To soup up a car or engine is to boost its performance, which is to improve or augment it.

clue.text: I say his cheque may bounce!

definitions.text: I say his cheque may bounce!

parts.words: I say his cheque may bounce!
parts.note: one who says things, and in law one who passes a forged or worthless cheque, an act called uttering

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims a warning that a man's cheque is likely to be dishonoured.
explanation.walkthrough: Uttering a forged document, such as a dud cheque, is a legal offence, so the person who says 'I say' and the forger share the name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a speaker, and legally a person who passes off counterfeit money or a forged cheque.

clue.text: Shrinking? Tense? I'm the same

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
taken as written, apostrophe dropped
id., short for idem, means the same in references

explanation.surface: A nervous person asks whether they are shrinking and tense, and admits to the same.
explanation.walkthrough: ID is the abbreviation of Latin idem, 'the same', used in footnotes.
explanation.definitionFit: A timid person shrinks back from danger, so shrinking is a synonym for lacking courage.

clue.text: So the poet shines once more on sick, sorry muse

definitions.text: So the poet shines once more

parts.note: re means on or concerning
ill means sick

indicators.note: a sorry state is a poor one, so the letters of muse are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: A poet, ill and feeling wretched, still finds his muse lighting him up again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorry' turns MUSE into UMES. 'So the poet' marks the definition as a poetic word.
explanation.definitionFit: To relume is a poetic verb for relighting, so a poet who lights again uses this word.

clue.text: Shed clue

parts.note: what you shed on a puzzle to clear it up, and also the crossword word for an entry in the grid

explanation.definitionFit: To shed this on a matter is to illuminate it, and in crosswords the word names a grid entry.

clue.text: No love letters from him: a late developer

indicators.note: a developer reworks and changes things, so these letters are rebuilt into a new order

explanation.surface: A man who matures late in life is no writer of romantic letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developer' signals the anagram of HIM A LATE; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Abusive letters expressing loathing are the opposite of love letters.

clue.text: Sturm und Drang applied to mopheads?

definitions.text: Sturm und Drang applied to mopheads?

parts.words: Sturm und Drang applied to mopheads?
parts.note: storm and stress inflicted on people with a thick mass of hair, a mass called a shock

explanation.surface: German romantic turmoil is visited upon shaggy-haired people.
explanation.walkthrough: Sturm und Drang ('storm and stress') was a German literary movement; a shock is also a thick mop of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggressive methods meant to stun opponents are the violent turmoil the German phrase suggests.

clue.text: Some unspecified support from politician involved in Manhattan Project

indicators.note: one piece is wrapped up within another, as something involved in a scheme sits inside it

parts.note: the United Nations, whose headquarters project stands in Manhattan, is UN
MP, Member of Parliament
a tee supports a golf ball

explanation.surface: A politician gives vague backing to the wartime atomic bomb programme.
explanation.walkthrough: The Manhattan Project was the atomic bomb effort, but here it means the UN, based in Manhattan. 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is informal for a large but indefinite number, a quantity left unspecified.

clue.text: Santa's helper having a day with Comic Relief?

definitions.text: Santa's helper having a day with Comic Relief?

parts.words: Santa's helper having a day with Comic Relief?
parts.note: the reindeer famous for a red nose would be at home on Red Nose Day, the charity's fundraising day

explanation.surface: Father Christmas's assistant joins in the charity comedy fundraiser.
explanation.walkthrough: Comic Relief is a British charity whose fundraiser, Red Nose Day, has people wear red clown noses.
explanation.definitionFit: The red-nosed reindeer of the song pulls Santa's sleigh, making him a seasonal helper.

clue.text: Yale key locked in his university admissions

annotationWithheld.why: Yale key locked in his university admissions (5): ELI (a Yale man) + HU (first letters of his university) builds the answer, but then Yale must also serve in the definition (Elihu Yale), one word doing two jobs, and 'locked in' has no container role
annotationWithheld.clue: Yale key locked in his university admissions

clue.text: Lover yielding up a pitch to 26

indicators.note: in a down answer, giving up means the whole sequence is turned to read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: tar is black pitch
the answer to 26 across, an Arab of Oman

explanation.surface: A lover concedes a playing field to a man from Oman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yielding up' turns A TAR OMANI, read upwards, into the answer; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian-derived word means a female lover or sweetheart.

clue.text: Harmonious Mercury hit, one side scratched, unfortunately

indicators.note: scratched means struck out, so one letter is removed
an unfortunate turn of events leaves these letters jumbled

parts.note: R is right, one side

explanation.surface: A planet or messenger god takes a hit and has one flank scraped, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scratched' removes R (right) from MERCURY HIT, and 'unfortunately' shuffles the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhythmical and harmonious in movement are the senses of this word, as in graceful dance.

clue.text: Lens capturing some pachyderm in toto

indicators.note: one word captures another by holding it inside

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: only some of the word is used, its start without the tail

parts.note: an elephant is a pachyderm

explanation.surface: A camera lens captures an elephant entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in toto' reads as Latin for entirely, but the toto is the container; 'some' trims the beast to its first five letters, and 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephoto is a camera lens that magnifies distant subjects.

clue.text: Principal leading impulsively

parts.note: a head is a school principal
first means leading

explanation.surface: A school principal rushes in ahead of everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Diving in with the head foremost suggests rushing ahead rashly, without thinking.

clue.text: Name a Tudor king climbing on the rocks

indicators.note: in a down answer, climbing reads the letters upwards

parts.note: to cite is to name
HR, Henricus Rex, King Henry, as Tudor monarchs signed

explanation.surface: A Tudor monarch is named as one scaling a cliff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reverses CITE A HR; 'on the' is a link. HR is Henry Rex, the Tudor royal signature.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names a group of rock strata at the top of the Triassic, a geological series.

clue.text: Linesman at Alice's croquet match

parts.note: not an official on the touchline but the artist whose lines pictured the Queen's croquet game in Wonderland

explanation.surface: An official watches the boundary at Alice's flamingo croquet game.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir John Tenniel drew the original illustrations for Alice's Adventures in Wonderland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian illustrator drew the croquet scene with flamingos and hedgehogs in Lewis Carroll's book.

clue.text: Composer with acoustic pitch

indicators.note: acoustic refers to sound, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a ship lists or pitches when it tilts

explanation.surface: A musician of the acoustic guitar knows pitch well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' looks musical but means a lean, LIST. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was the Hungarian Romantic pianist and composer.

clue.text: Companion left between love and time of affection

parts.note: CH, Companion of Honour

indicators.note: the letter goes in between two pieces

parts.note: love is zero, O, in tennis
an era is a period of time
L is left

explanation.surface: A companion leaves amid love and a time of tenderness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affection' looks like fondness but is the old medical sense, a disease. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In older medical usage an affection is a disease or disorder of the body.

clue.text: Top oneself? Close thing!

parts.note: to close is to end
it, a thing

explanation.surface: Someone at a high point declares a near miss.
explanation.definitionFit: To top oneself is British slang for suicide, ending it all.

clue.text: Relatively indulgent over free credit, say

indicators.note: turned over, the letters run backwards

parts.note: open means free

indicators.note: say means the word is spoken, so its sound counts

parts.note: on tick means on credit

explanation.surface: A generous relative goes over free credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses OPEN to NEPO, and 'say' gives the sound of TICK, credit, as TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepotism is favouritism to relatives, so this word means indulgent towards kin.

clue.text: Article carried by another clan chieftain

indicators.note: one piece is carried within another

parts.note: another article, the definite one, the
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece is carried by a different clan leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' means another article, so THE carries AN.
explanation.definitionFit: A thane was a Scottish clan chief or lord, like Macbeth.

clue.text: Outlaws outlaw song spiel!

parts.note: to ban is to outlaw

indicators.note: a spiel is patter, spoken talk, so the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a ditty is a song

explanation.surface: Bandits ban a song's patter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outlaw' is a verb, BAN; 'spiel' says DITTY as DITTI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian plural means bandits, outlaws.

clue.text: "No man is an island"? This Arab's surrounded!

indicators.note: the letters sit surrounded by the words of the quotation

explanation.surface: Donne's line about no man being an island is applied to an Arab boxed in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounded' signals the run hidden in NO MAN IS; ''s' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Oman is an Arab.

clue.text: Ballot fixers in attractive colours, not our problem

indicators.note: not means leave out these letters
a problem jumbles letters

explanation.surface: Election riggers wear pleasing colours and say it is not their business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not our' removes OUR from ATTRACTIVE COLOURS, and 'problem' shuffles the rest; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactical voters choose candidates strategically, fixing a ballot outcome.
